method_card.title: Daily Routine and Home Life
method_card.content:
This lesson covers reflexive verbs for daily routines and time expressions used to describe life at home.

FrenchEnglish
se leverto get up
se coucherto go to bed
se laverto wash / have a wash
se brosser les dentsto brush one's teeth
se réveillerto wake up
s'habillerto get dressed
se détendreto relax
se reposerto rest
prendre le petit déjeunerto have breakfast
rentrer à la maisonto go home
tôtearly
tardlate
d'abordfirst of all
ensuitethen / next
enfinfinally

Reflexive verbs have an extra pronoun that matches the subject: me (je), te (tu), se (il/elle/on), nous (nous), vous (vous), se (ils/elles). The pronoun goes before the verb: Je me lève à sept heures = I get up at seven o'clock. Il se couche tard = He goes to bed late. In negatives, ne…pas surrounds the pronoun and the verb: Je ne me couche pas tard = I don't go to bed late.

Time expressions: use à + time (à sept heures), le matin (in the morning), le soir (in the evening), d'abord…ensuite…enfin to sequence your routine.

Model: Le matin, je me réveille à six heures et demie. D'abord je me lève, ensuite je me brosse les dents et je m'habille. Le soir, je me détends et je me couche à dix heures. — In the morning, I wake up at half past six. First I get up, then I brush my teeth and get dressed. In the evening, I relax and go to bed at ten o'clock.
steps: Learn the reflexive verb forms for daily routine activities
Master the reflexive pronouns (me, te, se, nous, vous, se) and their positions
Practice sequencing your routine using d'abord, ensuite, enfin
Write full sentences combining reflexive verbs and time expressions

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — daily routine appears across speaking, listening and writing tasks

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Je me lève à sept heures et je me brosse les dents.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break the sentence into chunks: Je me lève | à sept heures | et | je me brosse les dents.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Je me lève = I get up (reflexive verb se lever, je form). à sept heures = at seven o'clock.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: je me brosse les dents = I brush my teeth (reflexive verb se brosser).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I get up at seven o'clock and I brush my teeth.

worked_examples.question: How do reflexive verbs work in French? Show the rule with se lever.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: A reflexive verb has a pronoun that matches the subject: je me lève, tu te lèves, il/elle se lève.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The pronoun goes before the verb, not after. Never say je lève me.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: In negatives, ne…pas wraps around both the pronoun and the verb: je ne me lève pas tôt.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Subject + reflexive pronoun + verb. Je me lève, tu te lèves, il/elle se lève, nous nous levons, vous vous levez, ils/elles se lèvent.

bronze.question: Match the French reflexive verbs to the English meaning
Match the French time expressions to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct reflexive pronoun

gaps.correct_explain: me is the reflexive pronoun for je. Je me réveille = I wake up.
te is the reflexive pronoun for tu. Tu te lèves = You get up.
se is the reflexive pronoun for il/elle. Elle se couche = She goes to bed.
lève is the je form of se lever. Note the grave accent: lève.

wrong.lever: lever is the infinitive. You need the conjugated form: je me lève.

gaps.correct_explain: dents = teeth. Se brosser les dents = to brush one's teeth.

wrong.cheveux: cheveux means hair, not teeth. Les dents = teeth.

gaps.correct_explain: habille is the je form of s'habiller. Je m'habille = I get dressed.

wrong.habiller: habiller is the infinitive. You need the conjugated form: je m'habille.

bronze.question: What does 'Je me couche à dix heures du soir' mean?
options: I go to bed at ten o'clock in the evening
I get up at ten o'clock in the evening
I go to bed at ten o'clock in the morning
She goes to bed at ten o'clock

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'He gets up early'?

bronze.source_text: Le matin, je me réveille à sept heures et je prends le petit déjeuner.
model_answers: In the morning, I wake up at seven o'clock and I have breakfast.
In the morning, I wake up at seven o'clock and I eat breakfast.
hints: je me réveille = I wake up
prendre le petit déjeuner = to have breakfast

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct reflexive verb form
silver.english: She relaxes after school and she goes to bed at half past ten.
sentence_parts: après le collège et elle se

gaps.correct_explain: détend is the elle form of se détendre. Elle se détend = She relaxes.

wrong.détendre: détendre is the infinitive. You need the conjugated form: elle se détend.
wrong.détends: détends is the je/tu form. For elle, use détend (no final -s).

gaps.correct_explain: couche is the elle form of se coucher. Elle se couche = She goes to bed.

wrong.coucher: coucher is the infinitive. You need the conjugated form: couche.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Mon frère se lève à sept heures et il me brosse les dents.
silver.explanation: The subject is il (mon frère), so the reflexive pronoun must be se, not me. Il se brosse les dents.
silver.translation: My brother gets up at seven o'clock and he brushes his teeth.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: Every morning, I get up and I have a wash.

distractor_labels.te: wrong pronoun — the subject is je (I), so the reflexive pronoun is me, not te

silver.source_text: In the evening, I relax and I go to bed at nine o'clock.
model_answers: Le soir, je me détends et je me couche à neuf heures.
hints: to go to bed = se coucher

gold.question: Build the sentence in French
gold.english: First she gets up, then she washes and gets dressed.

distractor_labels.me: wrong pronoun — the subject is elle, so the reflexive pronoun is se, not me
distractor_labels.te: wrong pronoun — the subject is elle, so the reflexive pronoun is se, not te
distractor_labels.lever: infinitive form — you need the conjugated elle form: lève, not lever

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a leisure centre in France. The receptionist asks you about your weekly routine and healthy habits.

bullets.prompt: Say what time you get up during the week and how you start your day.
bullets.model_answer: En semaine, je me lève à sept heures. D'abord je me lave et je m'habille, ensuite je prends le petit déjeuner.
bullets.note: reflexive verbs: se lever, se laver, s'habiller + sequencing: d'abord…ensuite

bullets.prompt: Say what you do in the evening to relax and when you go to bed.
bullets.model_answer: Le soir, je me détends en lisant ou en regardant la télévision. Je me couche à dix heures.
bullets.note: se détendre + en + present participle; se coucher + time

bullets.prompt: Ask the receptionist what activities the leisure centre offers at the weekend.
bullets.model_answer: Quelles activités est-ce que le centre propose le week-end, s'il vous plaît ?
bullets.note: question formation: quelles + noun + est-ce que; polite register

bullets.prompt: Say that you would like to do swimming regularly to stay fit.
bullets.model_answer: Je voudrais faire de la natation régulièrement pour garder la forme.
bullets.note: je voudrais (conditional = polite) + faire de la natation + garder la forme

gaps.correct_explain: levais is the imperfect of se lever. In si clauses with a conditional result, use the imperfect.

wrong.lèverais: After si, you cannot use the conditional. Use the imperfect: levais.
wrong.lève: lève is present tense. A si clause hypothesising about the present/future uses the imperfect.

gaps.correct_explain: serais is the conditional of être. The result clause of a si + imperfect structure uses the conditional.

wrong.suis: suis is present tense. The result clause needs the conditional: serais.
wrong.étais: étais is imperfect. The result clause needs the conditional: serais.
